scope: Provenance and declared-claim gate for MicroProxy V0-V8. Functional source proofs under explicit compiler/runtime/provider/facade trust are distinct from model proofs, finite tests, historical bytecode snapshots, blocked alternate routes and deferred timing/expert work. This ledger never proves the mathematics itself.

dafny-toolchain.statement: Dafny 4.9.1 and Z3 4.12.1 implementation correctness; official archive bytes are pinned and checked.

dafny-runtime.statement: The pinned Maven DafnyRuntime 4.9.1 jar is trusted and differs from the compiler-bundled runtime; byte differences are not assumed away.

javac-jvm.statement: javac and JVM correctness, including exact class/JAR delivery; no JIT/CPU timing property is assumed.

jdk-primitives.statement: Selected JDK SHA-2/SHA-3/HMAC/AEAD/classical providers implement their documented primitives; entropy and cryptographic hardness are separate assumptions.

generated-runtime-discipline.statement: Reviewed generated-runtime/bytecode metadata boundaries hold for the pinned emitted graph; this is not a whole-program noninterference or timing theorem.

reviewed-java-facades.statement: The small handwritten Shake and ML-KEM facades are reviewed and tested adapters, not Dafny-proved code.

packet-compiler-lowering.statement: The packet component trusts exactly two documented bounded-shift compiler lowerings; all other compiler output is not rewritten.

saw-toolchain.statement: SAW/Crucible bytecode semantics/translation, Cryptol, the bundled solver and the selected JDK class-file model are trusted.

lean-toolchain.statement: Lean 4.35.0 kernel checking and the explicitly allowed standard axioms are trusted; untrusted axioms/holes/native evaluation are rejected by the runner.

tlc-finite-model.statement: TLC exhaustively explores only the configured finite caps; this is bounded model checking, not unbounded refinement.

crypto-hardness-entropy.statement: Cryptographic hardness, PRF/PRP/entropy and security reductions are assumptions; functional proofs do not imply them.

jvm-timing-jit-cpu-gc.statement: HotSpot/JIT, CPU, GC, provider and physical-erasure timing are outside the proofs; local samples are observations, not a constant-time theorem.

trusted-bytecode-mapper-policy.statement: The javap-based extractor, CFG/taint/dispatch policy mapping and certificate emitter are trusted reviewed code, mutation-tested but not formally verified; certificate semantics are not JVM value/timing semantics.

assumed-owned-helper-trace-contracts.statement: The five checked caller certificates assume 19 opaque owned helper/adapter trace contracts; every assumed target remains in the unchecked-owned inventory and is not a provider or proved callee.

trusted-source-observation-coverage.statement: The reviewed C# adapter over the official resolved Dafny AST faithfully checks observation coverage, metadata and append/callee order for the supported HKDF source language. It is mutation-tested trusted code, not a formally verified execution semantics or a JVM trace refinement.

obligations.title: Secret-trace proof for our code
obligations.statement: The actual production HKDF Dafny methods have scoped paired source-trace proofs (248 body/259 paired-domain checks) with the separately trusted resolved-AST coverage adapter, 72 control records and byte-identical generated Java/classes. Full native SHAKE/Keccak/NTT/KEM and adapter/comparison trace composition remains open. Conditional trace evidence covers the original five callers, four codec helpers, two static HKDF helper roots, nine NativeField helpers, a separate composed Feed and seven fully expanded Keccak helpers under explicit mapper/runtime/provider assumptions. The Keccak concrete programs prove public-only scalar arguments, exact argument counts, no heap arguments and known targets for their remaining provider calls. Completed finite controls enforce public-heap equality and all 24 permutation rounds. The original caller set retains 19 assumed owned contracts; 13 roots and 31 aggregate labels remain open. Copy/alias, JVM value/timing and full V7 closure are not claimed. Select adds a separately gated source slice over fixed public shapes, legal aliases and a fresh output; its logical observations do not establish whole-KEM or physical JVM trace independence.

limitations: No complete secret-trace proof covers HKDF, SHAKE or ML-KEM.
Packet trace observer excludes JIT/CPU/GC/provider timing, ByteBuffer internals, downstream AEAD/metadata and outbound protection.
No JVM/machine-code timing theorem or whole-record constant-time claim exists.
Finite timing samples are not pass/fail evidence.
The timing component has 13 open owned roots and 19 assumed owned helper/adapter trace contracts; every assumed target remains in the checked unchecked-owned inventory.

Five actual-bytecode caller certificates are conditional on the trusted javap extractor/policy and abstract SecretTrace semantics; they do not prove JVM value refinement, implicit exceptions or timing.
Packet receive trace remains separately scoped; this does not promote the whole V7 obligation.
The Keccak supplement excludes the Permute wrapper, Sponge ownership/NI and full polynomial/NTT/KEM and adapter trace composition; receiver prototypes are outside accepted evidence.
The shared public oracle is an abstract pure deterministic contract; its checked public-argument premise is not a proof of JDK/provider internals, JVM narrowing, implicit exceptions or timing.

obligations.title: Runtime evidence and assurance release gate
obligations.statement: The non-timing release gate consumes the V0 ledger, validates exactly supported functional claims, and reports residual deferred/blocked claims; runtime timing manifests, deployment machine-code inspection and independent expert review remain open.

evidence.role: fail-closed obligation ledger validator
claim-level release gate

ledger status, renewal and residual guide

timing limitations
published claim scope and residual limits
historical local artifact acceptance
historical bundle comparison
current delivery/runtime pins
current generated-source/class inventory
fresh actual-artifact orchestration and end-of-run bindings
actual-artifact gate regression and rejection controls

limitations: The historical adoption JAR/bundle receipts cannot authenticate a fresh current full JAR.
No pinned multi-JDK/CPU timing manifest or statistical pass/fail claim is provided.
No independent external cryptographic/proof review exists.
No generic whole-proxy "secure" claim follows from the ledger.

claims.statement: Production SHAKE128/256 and ML-KEM-768 use Java generated from functionally verified Dafny and delivered through the pinned generated-source/class inventory, under the listed compiler/runtime/provider/facade trust assumptions.
limitations: Functional equations only; no cryptographic-hardness, JVM-timing or physical-erasure claim.
Historical whole-JAR receipts are not fresh current-release identity evidence.

claims.statement: The current local generated-Java Dafny HKDF kernel meets its stated Extract/Expand/TLS-label result equations relative to deterministic abstract HMAC over its general public domain, with exact generated-source/class binding and real-JCE adapter tests; it does not include a verified AWS dependency closure.
limitations: V1 remains partial because the AWS full dependency closure failed; target-only success is not closure.
Adapters, compiler/runtime and JCE provider are trusted and tested, not proved; this is not an adapter refinement theorem.
No full-JAR identity, whole-bytecode equivalence, timing or security proof.

claims.statement: Production quic.Hkdf conditionally implements the verified local Dafny HKDF equations through the generated package, reviewed HkdfBridge and exact JdkHmac provider leaf, under explicit compiler/runtime/provider/facade trust; this is a component functional/production claim, not full-JAR identity or whole-bytecode equivalence.
limitations: Component functional/generation claim only; no fresh full-JAR identity, whole-bytecode equivalence, adapter refinement, timing or security proof.
V1 remains partial because the AWS full dependency closure failed.

claims.statement: Historical pre-adoption Java 21 MlKem768.reduceOnce bytecode satisfies a mod-3329 result for 0 <= a < 6658.
limitations: Historical reference class, not current generated NativeField.
Callers, other ML-KEM operations and timing are outside the proof.

claims.statement: Actual PacketKey.nonce(long) bytecode is proved equivalent to the intended nonce construction for all IV and packet-number bits.
limitations: Blocked by unsupported primitive-array clone translation; no clone contract or result was admitted.

claims.statement: The portable SAW/Crucible array-clone route is selected and complete for the nonce bridge.
limitations: This alternate route is not complete; the selected implementation route is generated Dafny Java.

claims.statement: The adopted production PacketKey.nonce delegates to the Dafny-verified generated VerifiedNonce primitive: the same frozen source is audited/proved with five genuine proof-obligation rejects before bounded --no-verify generation, the checked-in generated source/class is bound by GENERATED.json and the central delivery inventory, and PacketKey.seal/open plus nonce vectors pass on JDK 21 and JDK 25. This is a functional component claim only.
limitations: Functional nonce primitive and PacketKey delegation only; no cryptographic hardness, PRF/entropy, side-channel or constant-time claim.
The historical SAW PacketKey.nonce bytecode route remains blocked; this claim is a separate generated functional route.
No JVM timing/capacity claim; the packet benchmark is diagnostic shared-host evidence.
No current full-JAR or deployment identity claim; that still requires fresh canonical stage and actual-artifact validation.
Dafny/Boogie/Z3, Dafny Java compiler/runtime, javac, JVM/JCE providers and archive extraction remain trusted.

claims.statement: A paired-run atomic-word/register trace model applies to actual packet receive scalar classes for the documented receive-path observer, with fixed-address adapters and structural/taint checks.
limitations: Scoped receive-path source/bytecode trace only; excludes JIT/CPU/GC/provider timing and downstream record processing.
Does not complete V7 for HKDF, SHAKE or ML-KEM.

claims.statement: The ledger/release gate rejects stale, incomplete, vacuous, finite-only, misclassified-control, model-only-production, broad-security/timing/expert and deferred-as-done claims while allowing honest residual reporting.
limitations: The gate validates provenance and declared claims, not the mathematical proofs themselves.
It does not make timing or expert-review evidence exist.

claims.statement: Pinned multi-JDK/CPU runtime manifests, machine-code/intrinsic inspection and statistically justified timing conclusions support a release timing claim.
limitations: Only raw opt-in local observations exist; no pass/fail threshold or deployment machine-code proof.

claims.statement: A fresh receipt binds the current release full JAR/class entries to the verified generated-source graph at the current revision.
limitations: Existing acceptance/final-bundle receipts pre-date current main and cannot authenticate a fresh current full JAR.

claims.statement: Historical local acceptance compared generated crypto classes and a minimized bundle at the recorded adoption stage.
limitations: Snapshot only; matching historical hashes do not authenticate the current JAR or constitute semantic proof.

claims.statement: Independent external cryptographic/proof experts reviewed the current proofs, implementation and claims.
limitations: Only agent-assisted development review exists; no independent external audit is claimed.

claims.statement: The cryptographic constructions are proved secure under a named reduction and adversary model.
limitations: Functional proofs do not imply cryptographic hardness or security reductions.

claims.statement: The deployed JVM/JIT/CPU/provider implementation is constant time for all secret-dependent operations.
limitations: JVM/CPU/GC/provider timing is explicitly deferred; no constant-time claim is supported.

claims.statement: The whole MicroProxy is proved secure.
limitations: No end-to-end security proof, protocol refinement or independent audit exists.

claims.statement: The full AWS MPL upstream HKDF dependency/submodule graph was independently replayed for this repository.
limitations: Only the standalone local kernel was verified; upstream provenance is attribution for reused structure, not a full graph replay.

claims.statement: The adopted NativeField/NativePolynomial Dafny source carries paired ghost observation proofs for 20 resolved method roots and 19 executable pure functions (including forward/inverse NTT and multiplication), whose observations are bound by a separately trusted resolved-AST checker to the actual operations, resolved callees and trace outputs. The reviewed root identities, ambient-selector clearing, repeated-root rejection and negative controls are gated from the actual portable-package report; the claim is scoped to this source component and does not extend to Keccak/Shake, full ML-KEM composition, adapters, invalid-input paths, physical memory or issue #117.
limitations: The C# resolved-AST checker and the Dafny parser/compiler/verifier are trusted; this does not prove the checker or compiler correct.
Read/write observations are method-local resolved roles and indices, not physical Java heap addresses or an erasure model.
No JVM/JIT/CPU timing or constant-time claim, and no bytecode-level refinement beyond the recorded ghost-erasure class-identity check.
Keccak/Shake, full ML-KEM composition, adapter/invalid-input trace composition and the KeyGen rho-failure NI path remain open; this does not close issue #117.
The Linux 14-control replay and the release/nonce gates are separate; this claim covers only the reviewed source roots and controls.

claims.statement: The actual NativeMlKem.Select Dafny method returns a fresh 32-byte result, preserves its existing-heap frame and permitted aliases, and proves equal logical source observations for fixed public shapes/ciphertext while expected/candidate/fallback byte contents vary. A separately trusted resolved-AST checker binds observations to actual operations and the sole result allocation. The same-source generation has exact ghost erasure for 65 algorithm Java files/classes on JDK 21/25 under both reviewed Mac and Linux profiles. This is a Select source slice, not whole ML-KEM trace composition or physical JVM security.
limitations: The C# coverage checker, Python orchestration/evidence validator and Dafny/Boogie/Z3 toolchain remain trusted; this does not formally prove the checker or compiler correct.
Read/write roles and indices are method-local logical identities, not physical Java heap addresses, JVM timing or physical erasure.
Compiler/runtime/provider correctness and whole-KEM, SHAKE/Keccak, adapter, invalid-input and rho-failure trace composition remain open; this does not close issue #117.
Independent external cryptographic/proof review and cryptographic security reductions remain open.
The 65-class component erasure and 66-class complete delivery inventories have different scopes; supplied-artifact checks remain separate.

claims.statement: Every V0-V8 obligation, including production HKDF adoption, complete secret-trace/timing evidence, fresh current-JAR identity and independent expert review, is closed.
limitations: Deferred/blocked/unsupported residuals remain; --require-all must fail until they are genuinely closed.
